questions.enonce_markdown: The sum of the first and second terms of a geometric progression is $-5$ while the sum of the fourth and fifth terms of the same progression is $40$. Find the first term and common ratio of the progression. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let the first term be $a$ and the common ratio $r$. The terms are $a, ar, ar^2, ar^3, ar^4, \dots$

$$a + ar = -5 \;\Rightarrow\; a(1 + r) = -5, \qquad \text{(1)}$$
$$ar^3 + ar^4 = 40 \;\Rightarrow\; ar^3(1 + r) = 40. \qquad \text{(2)}$$

From (1), $a(1 + r) \neq 0$, so we may divide (2) by (1):
$$\frac{ar^3(1+r)}{a(1+r)} = \frac{40}{-5} \;\Rightarrow\; r^3 = -8 \;\Rightarrow\; r = -2$$
(the only real cube root of $-8$).

Substitute in (1): $a(1 - 2) = -5 \Rightarrow -a = -5 \Rightarrow a = 5$.

$$\boxed{a = 5, \qquad r = -2}$$

**Check.** The terms are $5, -10, 20, -40, 80, \dots$ First + second $= 5 - 10 = -5$; fourth + fifth $= -40 + 80 = 40$.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(x + \dfrac{2}{x^2}\right)^{15}$. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The general term in the binomial expansion of $\left(x + \dfrac{2}{x^2}\right)^{15}$ is
$$T_{r+1} = \binom{15}{r} x^{15 - r}\left(\frac{2}{x^2}\right)^r = \binom{15}{r}\, 2^r\, x^{15 - r - 2r} = \binom{15}{r}\, 2^r\, x^{15 - 3r}.$$
The term is independent of $x$ when the power of $x$ is zero:
$$15 - 3r = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; r = 5.$$
This is the sixth term:
$$T_6 = \binom{15}{5}\, 2^5 = 3003 \times 32 = 96\,096.$$
$$\boxed{\text{The term independent of } x \text{ is } 96\,096}$$
